title: Making Plans
description: Learn to make invitations and social plans
objectives: Make invitations (Do you want to...? / Would you like to...?)
Decline politely (I can't, sorry / Maybe next time)
Talk about future plans (I'm going to...)

target_language.grammar_pattern:
Invitations:
- Do you want to + verb?
- Would you like to + verb?

Accepting:
- Sure! / Yes! / That sounds great!

Declining:
- Sorry, I can't
- I'm busy
- Maybe another time

Future:
- I'm going to + verb
- I'm + verb-ing (planned)

Examples:
- Do you want to get coffee?
- Sure! When?
- I'm busy on Saturday
- I'm going to the movies

grammar_patterns.label: Making invitations
examples: Do you want to get coffee?
Do you want to see a movie?
Do you want to go shopping?

grammar_patterns.label: Declining politely
grammar_patterns.pattern: I can't, sorry. / Maybe next time.

story.context: You want to hang out with your friend Lisa. You try to make plans.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi Lisa! Do you want to get coffee this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Are you free on Saturday afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Saturday? Let me check... Sorry, I can't. I'm busy on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Perfect! Where do you want to meet?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: At the cafe on Main Street?

dialogue.speaker: Lisa
dialogue.text: Sounds good! See you Sunday at 2!

listening.question: Listen: When does Ahmed want to meet?
listening.transcript: Saturday doesn't work for me. Can we meet on Sunday instead?
listening.explanation: Ahmed suggests Sunday after Saturday doesn't work

listening.question: Listen: Can Lisa meet on Saturday?
listening.transcript: Can you meet on Saturday, Lisa? No, I'm busy on Saturday.

listening.question: Listen: What time will they meet?

speaking.title: Task 1: Make an invitation
speaking.instruction: Record yourself inviting someone to get coffee on Saturday.
speaking.example: Hi! Do you want to get coffee this Saturday? Are you free in the afternoon? Maybe around 2 PM?

speaking.title: Task 2: Accept and decline
speaking.instruction: Record yourself accepting one invitation and declining another.
speaking.example:
Person: Do you want to see a movie?
You: Sure! That sounds great! When?
---
Person: Do you want to have dinner on Monday?
You: I'm sorry, I can't. I'm busy on Monday. Maybe next week?

writing.title: Task 1: Plan a get-together
writing.instruction: Write a text message inviting a friend to do something. Include: activity, day, time, and place.
writing.example: Hi! Do you want to see a movie this Saturday? There's a new action movie at the theater. How about 7 PM? We can meet at the theater on Main Street. Let me know!

writing.title: Task 2: Make plans conversation
writing.instruction: Write a conversation (10-12 lines) where you invite someone, they're busy, you suggest another day, and they accept.
writing.example:
You: Hi! Do you want to go shopping on Saturday?
Friend: Saturday? I can't, sorry. I'm busy.
You: Oh okay. What about Sunday?
Friend: Sunday works! What time?
You: How about 2 PM?
Friend: Perfect! Where?
You: At the mall?
Friend: Sounds good!
You: Great! See you Sunday at 2.
Friend: See you then!

sections.title: Do you want to vs Would you like to
examples: Do you want to get coffee? (casual, with friends)
Would you like to have dinner? (more polite, formal)
sections.question: What's the difference?
sections.explanation: 'Do you want to' is casual and common with friends. 'Would you like to' is more polite and formal, good for new acquaintances or professional situations.

sections.title: Declining politely
examples: I'd love to, but I can't (shows interest)
sections.question: How do we say no politely?
sections.explanation: In English, we soften rejection by: apologizing ('sorry'), giving a reason ('I'm busy'), or suggesting alternatives ('maybe next time'). This is more polite than just 'no'.

sections.title: Future plans: I'm going to vs I'm -ing
examples: I'm going to see a movie (intention, plan)
I'm seeing a movie on Saturday (definite arrangement)
What are you doing Saturday? (asking about plans)
sections.question: How do we talk about future plans?
sections.explanation: Both work! 'I'm going to' expresses intention. 'I'm -ing' (present continuous) is used for definite plans/arrangements.

quiz.question: You want to invite a friend to coffee. What do you say?
options: Do you want to get coffee?
quiz.explanation: 'Do you want to get coffee?' is the correct invitation.

quiz.question: Someone invites you to dinner and you want to accept. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'Sure! That sounds great!' is enthusiastic and clear acceptance.

quiz.question: You can't accept an invitation. What is the MOST polite way to decline?
options: I'm busy, sorry. Maybe next time?
quiz.explanation: Giving a reason and suggesting another time is most polite.

quiz.question: You want to know if someone is available on Saturday. What do you ask?
quiz.explanation: 'Are you free on Saturday?' is the correct question.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: Do you want ___ a movie?
quiz.explanation: After 'want', we use 'to + verb'. 'Do you want to see a movie?' is correct.

quiz.question: Someone asks 'What are you doing Saturday?' They want to know:
quiz.explanation: This question asks about your plans/schedule for the upcoming Saturday.

quiz.question: Which is MORE polite?
options: Do you want to have dinner?
Would you like to have dinner?
quiz.explanation: 'Would you like to' is more polite and formal than 'Do you want to'.

quiz.question: Someone suggests meeting at 3 PM and you agree. What do you say?
quiz.explanation: 'Perfect! See you at 3' confirms the time and shows you're committed.

quiz.question: Write a conversation (6-8 lines) where you invite someone to see a movie, but they're busy. Suggest another day.
quiz.explanation: Include: invitation, decline with reason, alternative suggestion, acceptance, details (time/place).

quiz.question: When someone invites you but you're busy, how do you decline politely in your culture? Is it similar to English?
quiz.explanation: Think about cultural differences in politeness and declining invitations.
